ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, A, B, E, F, C are on the circumference, and in circumferential order they can be regarded as A-B-E-F-C. Point G is inside the circle and is the intersection point of chord FB and chord CE. The figure also shows two secants drawn from external point D, but the calculation in this problem mainly uses the relationships of intersecting chords inside a circle and inscribed angles. Reasoning: It is known that m arc FE=118, m arc AB=108, m∠EGB=52, m∠EFB=30. Because ∠EFB is an inscribed angle, and its intercepted arc is arc EB, m arc EB=2×30=60. Also because chord FB and chord CE intersect at point G, the measure of ∠EGB is equal to half the sum of the two arcs EB and CF that it intercepts, so 52=(60+m arc CF)/2, giving 104=60+m arc CF, therefore m arc CF=44. The total arc measure of the circumference is 360, and in order there is arc AB+arc BE+arc EF+arc FC+arc CA=360, so 108+60+118+44+m arc AC=360, hence m arc AC=30.

method.method_draft: From the diagram, note that A, B, E, F, C lie on the circle in order around the circumference, with G inside the circle where chords FB and CE intersect. Read from the text: m arc FE = 118, m arc AB = 108, m angle EGB = 52, and m angle EFB = 30. Use the inscribed-angle theorem on angle EFB: it intercepts arc EB, so m arc EB = 2(30) = 60. Then use the intersecting-chords theorem at G: angle EGB equals one-half the sum of arcs EB and CF, so 52 = (60 + m arc CF)/2, giving m arc CF = 44. Finally sum the five arcs around the circle: arc AB + arc BE + arc EF + arc FC + arc CA = 360. Thus 108 + 60 + 118 + 44 + m arc AC = 360, so m arc AC = 30.

method.method_draft: From the diagram, identify G as the intersection of chords CE and FB. Angle EGB is adjacent to angle BGC because GE and GC are opposite rays on chord CE, so angle BGC = 180 - 52 = 128. Read from the diagram that angle BGC intercepts the two opposite arcs BC and FE under the intersecting-chords theorem, and that the minor arc BC is made of arcs BA and AC. Read from the text: m arc FE = 118 and m arc AB = 108. Apply the intersecting-chords theorem to angle BGC: 128 = (m arc BC + 118)/2, so m arc BC = 256 - 118 = 138. Since arc BC = arc BA + arc AC = 108 + arc AC, solve 108 + arc AC = 138, giving m arc AC = 30.
